background_story: Harlow was a free-spirited artist who had always been drawn to the unknown. Growing up, she felt an inexplicable sense of absence, as if a part of her was missing. This feeling fueled her creativity, driving her to create art that explored the themes of longing and disconnection. As she traveled the world, Harlow began to realize that the absence she felt was not just within herself, but also in the people and places she encountered. She documented her findings in a series of hauntingly beautiful photographs, capturing the empty spaces and forgotten corners of cities and landscapes. Her work gained international recognition, but Harlow's own sense of absence remained, a constant reminder of the mysteries that lay just beyond the edge of perception.
